                  Free music you can reuse

                  Full songs shared by their makers under open licences, streamed from the Internet Archive. Only items marked CC0, Public Domain or Creative Commons BY / BY-SA appear. Nothing is copied to this site, and the Internet Archive sees your browser when you use this tab.

                  Licence
                  Order

                    Before you reuse a song

                    The licence shown is the one the uploader declared to the Internet Archive, and uploaders can be wrong. Keys while a song plays: Space pauses, the left and right arrows skip 5 seconds, the comma and full stop skip 15 seconds, M mutes and unmutes, R restarts the song or track, the slash key jumps to the search box, H hides or shows the songs you have played, O opens the playing song's source page, C copies its credit line, U plays the next song you have not played, S plays a random song, V shows more songs, A turns Autoplay on or off, T changes the order, F changes the licence filter, Z undoes the last change shown in a message, Y copies the song's Internet Archive link, W copies a link to the search, E shows only songs you stopped partway, X hides or shows songs you have kept, I shows only songs added in the last year, B changes the sleep timer, P plays the list in order, D tells you how many songs are shown, played and kept (and how long you have listened this visit), J tells you what is playing, which track it is on, how far along it is, repeat, speed and mute, and what is up next, Q tells you its licence, L repeats the song, the minus and plus keys change the volume, the number keys 0 to 9 jump through the song, and > changes the speed. Always open the source page and read the licence terms before using a song in your own release. CC BY needs credit to the artist (use Copy credit). CC BY-SA needs credit and that you share your new work under the same terms. CC0 and Public Domain need neither. A cover song can still carry the original songwriter’s rights. This is general information, not legal advice.

                    Your shortlist

                        Artist facts (who they are, where they are from, their style) come from MusicBrainz, a free community music database. Similarity and release data come from Deezer. The Free music tab streams openly licensed music from the Internet Archive. Fan counts are Deezer followers as of the snapshot date below, so an artist can be bigger elsewhere. A new release here may be missing if Deezer has not listed it. Your shortlist, notes and settings stay only in this browser. Keyboard: press ? for the list of shortcuts, or . Only artists in this snapshot can be searched. If yours is missing, try a similar one.
